title: /runs/read serves the declared migration identifiers and the browser decoder preserves them
description:
SPIDR child of task-122b55fd2c284174876bd1d5573bdcc5, filed by architect-fa3a3e17 on 2026-09-06. That row's own title names two subjects - "declare migration identifiers through durable authority" AND "Runs reads" - and its description says "Scope is authoritative declaration and production read contract". Measured, those are far apart: the authority half touches the scheduler's frozen key roster, its canonical serialization, its digest binding and every compile/seal/replay consumer (10+ daemon files reference `nodeAuthorityHash`/`NodeDefinition` before the read contract is reached). The two together are well past a workable plan. THE PARENT KEEPS THE AUTHORITY (its DoD 1, 2, 3); this row takes the READ CONTRACT (its DoD 4).

dependsOn the parent, because a read cannot serve a member the authority has not yet declared.

THE GAP, MEASURED AT HEAD by architect-fa3a3e17:
- `apps/daemon/src/http/runs-read-contract.ts:76-94` carries no migration identifiers.
- `apps/control-room/src/live/live-runs.ts:58-72` likewise none.
So the declaration the parent lands is invisible to the browser until this row serves it.

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: the production `/runs/read` contract serving the declared identifiers for the CORRECT EXECUTION IDENTITY, and the browser's exact-key decoder preserving them.

FOUR PROPERTIES THE PARENT'S DoD 4 NAMES, all of them read-side and none of them obvious:
1. THE CORRECT EXECUTION IDENTITY. A declaration belongs to one node's execution, and the read must not attribute it to another.
2. NO SHARED-NODE-KEY CROSS-GOAL BLEED. Node keys are shared across goals; a read keyed on nodeKey alone will serve one goal's declaration on another goal's run. This is the defect most likely to pass a single-goal test.
3. TWO DECLARED IDENTIFIERS BOTH SURVIVE - a read that keeps only the first passes every single-identifier fixture.
4. MALFORMED WIRE FAILS CLOSED, with a stable code and layer.
AND: NO RECEIPT OWNERSHIP INFERRED BY MATCHING FILENAME OR SHA (parent rail 1). If the read cannot establish ownership from durable identity, it serves nothing rather than guessing.

NOT IN SCOPE: the declaration itself, the key roster, canonical serialization, the digest binding, schema versioning and compatibility - all the parent's. No UI wording or rendering: task-78eedd8ebc2b43c581ac21ea28648a9a owns that and renders via board-lanes.tsx (goal-nodes.tsx is only a wrapper).</description>
definitionOfDone: Production `/runs/read` serves the declared migration identifiers for the CORRECT EXECUTION IDENTITY, asserted against a declaration written through the parent's real authority path - not a hand-built frame and not a fixture that mints the member directly.

NO SHARED-NODE-KEY CROSS-GOAL BLEED: two goals whose runs share a nodeKey, only one of which declares identifiers, are asserted separately - the declaring goal serves them and the other serves none. A read keyed on nodeKey alone passes a single-goal test and fails this one, which is why it is its own clause.
TWO DECLARED IDENTIFIERS BOTH SURVIVE the read and the browser decoder, asserted by value and by count. A read or decoder that keeps only the first passes every single-identifier fixture.

THE BROWSER DECODER IS EXACT-KEY AND PRESERVES THE MEMBER: `apps/control-room/src/live/live-runs.ts` decodes it, an unknown key and a missing key each refuse with the specific code AND the layer that refused, and a MALFORMED wire fails closed rather than dropping the member silently.

A RUN WITH NO DECLARATION IS DISTINCT FROM ONE DECLARING NONE - carry the parent's UNKNOWN-vs-explicit-empty distinction through the wire and the decoder rather than collapsing both to an empty array. Assert both.

NO OWNERSHIP INFERRED FROM A FILENAME OR A SHA (parent rail 1). If durable identity does not establish which execution a declaration belongs to, serve nothing and refuse - assert that path rather than falling back to a match.

Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`. Root `pnpm test` covers no apps/** file, so say that rather than quoting a bare root count line.
taskRails: READ CONTRACT ONLY. The declaration, the key roster, canonical serialization, the digest binding and schema compatibility are the parent's (task-122b55fd). Touch none of packages/scheduler.
NO OWNERSHIP BY FILENAME OR SHA MATCH. Establish it from durable identity or serve nothing.
NO CROSS-GOAL BLEED. Node keys are shared across goals; key the read on the execution identity, not on nodeKey alone.
NO UI. Wording and rendering belong to task-78eedd8e, which renders via board-lanes.tsx.
EXACT-KEY DECODING with a stable code AND layer; a malformed wire fails closed rather than dropping the member.

implementationPlan.description:
MEASURE THE TWO PREREQUISITES BEFORE ANY EDIT. This row's dependsOn names task-122b55fd (authority) and task-75bff0c9 (the author that carries identifiers from planning source into the compiled node); at plan time BOTH were unmet. dependsOn gates the WORKING claim, so if you are reading this the runtime already believes they are DONE — verify it on disk anyway, because DoD 1 stands or falls on it.

Run and record:
- `git grep -rn "declaredMigrations" -- apps packages` — at plan time this returned hits ONLY under `packages/scheduler/src/node-authority/` and ZERO under `apps/`. You need at least one hit in the daemon's compile path (`apps/daemon/src/planning/v2-compiler/**`), which is what proves task-75bff0c9 landed and that a compiled node can actually carry the member.
- `grep -n "declaredMigrations" packages/scheduler/src/node-authority/node-authority-contract.ts` — expect `:193 readonly declaredMigrations?: readonly string[];`. That exact spelling is the contract; do not rename it.
- Confirm the read path still reaches it: `grep -n "nodeAuthority" packages/scheduler/src/graph-content-fields.ts` (expect `:82 readonly nodeAuthority: NodeAuthoritySection`) and `sed -n '78,105p' apps/daemon/src/http/runs-read.ts` (the `SealedNode` interface and `sealedNodesOf`, which is where the member is currently dropped).

IF `declaredMigrations` HAS NO `apps/` HIT: there is no real authority path to assert against. `moe.report_blocked` with blockedOnTaskIds ["task-122b55fd2c284174876bd1d5573bdcc5", "task-75bff0c9efc24daaad81ac81a373cd90"], quoting the grep. Do NOT hand-build an authority body, do NOT mint the member directly in a fixture, and do NOT narrow DoD 1 — all three are explicitly forbidden.

Also `git status --porcelain` the paths below and note any peer dirt without touching it. No files change in this step.

DAEMON CONTRACT: add the member to `RunNodeView` in `apps/daemon/src/http/runs-read-contract.ts` (the interface at :76-100, alongside the existing `criterionIds` / `dependsOn` / `nodeRef` members).

SHAPE, and it is the load-bearing decision of this row:

  /** Authored order, never sorted or deduped. `null` means the node's authority
   * body declares nothing at all (UNKNOWN); `[]` means the author declared none. */
  readonly declaredMigrations: readonly string[] | null;

REQUIRED, not optional, and ALWAYS EMITTED. The browser's `exactDataRecord` (live-runs.ts:125-145) rejects any object whose own-key count differs from its roster, so a row that omitted the key when the declaration is UNKNOWN would fail to decode ENTIRELY — the whole Runs read would go dark, not just this member. Carrying `null` on the wire is what lets DoD 5's UNKNOWN-vs-explicit-empty distinction survive a strictly-exact decoder.

Mirror the member into the local `SealedNode` interface at `runs-read.ts:78-85` in the same edit so the two shapes stay adjacent and reviewable.

DAEMON READ: populate the member in `sealedNodesOf` (`apps/daemon/src/http/runs-read.ts:87-105`) and carry it onto the emitted row (:221-255).

Source it from the `definition` the loop is ALREADY holding:
`declaredMigrations: definition.declaredMigrations === undefined ? null : Object.freeze([...definition.declaredMigrations])`

WHY THIS EXACT SHAPE, three reasons, all of them DoD clauses:
- `undefined -> null` is the UNKNOWN-vs-declared-none distinction (DoD 5). Do not use `?? []` — that collapses both and the parent's contract says `[]` is defaulted nowhere.
- The loop at :92 iterates `graph.content.nodeAuthority.definitions` INSIDE the per-graph body, and :100 already derives `nodeRef` there via `compiledExecutionRef(projectId, graph, definition.nodeKey)`. Reading the member off that same `definition` gives the CORRECT EXECUTION IDENTITY for free (DoD 1) and makes cross-goal bleed structurally impossible (DoD 2). **Do not build a nodeKey-keyed map** — that is the exact defect DoD 2 names, and it passes every single-goal test.
- Copy-and-freeze rather than aliasing the authority array, so a read cannot mutate durable content.

PRESERVE AUTHORED ORDER: no `.sort()`, no `Set`, no dedup. The parent made order content and bound it into the digest.

Ownership comes from `nodeRef` alone. Never infer it from a filename or a SHA (task rail 2 / DoD 6): if the definition is not in this graph's `definitions`, the node serves nothing.

DAEMON TESTS in `apps/daemon/src/http/runs-read.test.ts`, driven through the real authority path measured in step 1 — a compiled graph whose node authority genuinely carries the declaration, never a hand-built body. Four arms, one per property:

(a) CORRECT EXECUTION IDENTITY (DoD 1): a goal whose node declares two identifiers serves them on that node's `nodeRef` row.
(b) NO SHARED-NODE-KEY CROSS-GOAL BLEED (DoD 2) — the arm that matters most: build TWO goals whose runs share the SAME `nodeKey`, where only one declares. Assert separately that the declaring goal's row serves the identifiers AND that the other goal's row serves `null`. An implementation keyed on `nodeKey` alone passes (a) and fails this; that is why it is its own arm.
(c) TWO IDENTIFIERS BOTH SURVIVE, IN AUTHORED ORDER (DoD 3): assert `toEqual(["<first>", "<second>"])` — by value and in order, not `toHaveLength(2)`, which a reversing or deduping implementation would pass.
(d) UNKNOWN vs EXPLICIT-EMPTY (DoD 5): a node whose authority declares nothing serves `null`; a node that declared none serves `[]`. Assert both in the same test so the two cannot be collapsed.

Also backfill the one node literal in `apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/compiled-node-identity.test.ts` (it states `sharedKey:`, so it constructs a full node and will not typecheck without the new member).

DRILL EVERY ARM: mutate the production surface and confirm red — `?? []` instead of `null` must red (d); keying the projection on `nodeKey` must red (b); a `.sort()` must red (c). Restore and prove restoration with `git diff` (these paths are tracked).

BROWSER DECODER in `apps/control-room/src/live/live-runs.ts`. Three small edits, ~6 lines total — this file is 383 physical lines against the 400 hard cap, so keep it tight and do NOT add a paragraph comment.

1. `RunNodeView` (:58-72): add `readonly declaredMigrations: readonly string[] | null;` — same shape as the daemon contract.
2. The exact-key roster in `nodeOf` (:237-240): add `"declaredMigrations"` to the array, in alphabetical position beside `"criterionIds"`.
3. The decode in `nodeOf`: branch EXPLICITLY, and in this order —

     const declaredMigrations = record.declaredMigrations === null
       ? null : stringList(record.declaredMigrations);
     if (declaredMigrations === undefined) return null;   // shape guard

   then require it alongside the existing `if (criterionIds === null || dependsOn === null || review === null) return null;` guard, adapted so that `null` stays a LEGAL value for this member while a malformed one refuses.

WHY THE EXPLICIT null BRANCH (DoD 4's fail-closed clause, and the likeliest silent defect in this row): `stringList` (:176) returns `null` for "not an array", and the wire's UNKNOWN is ALSO `null`. Funnelling both through one helper makes a malformed value — a number, a nested array, a string — indistinguishable from UNKNOWN, and the member is silently dropped instead of refusing. Branch on the literal `null` first, then demand a real string array.

A missing or unknown key already refuses through `exactDataRecord`'s length-and-membership check with `RUNS_RESPONSE_INVALID` @ `CONTROL_ROOM_LIVE_RUNS` (:7-8, :122); do not add a second code.

CONTINGENCY: if the edit would push the file past 400 lines, extract `nodeOf` into a sibling module and declare that new path — do not shorten an existing comment to squeak under.

Add no `@moe/scheduler` import: this file is a standalone wire decoder (measured: control-room imports the package nowhere) and must stay one.

BROWSER TESTS in `apps/control-room/src/live/live-runs.test.ts`, plus the fixture backfill the required member forces.

ARMS (DoD 3, 4, 5):
(a) Two identifiers survive the decoder by value AND in authored order: `toEqual(["<first>", "<second>"])`.
(b) `declaredMigrations: null` on the wire decodes to `null` — and assert THE WHOLE NODE still decodes, not merely the member. This is the guard against the omitted-key trap: if UNKNOWN were ever encoded by omission, every node row would fail `exactDataRecord` and the Runs read would go dark.
(c) `[]` decodes to `[]`, distinct from (b). Assert both in one test so they cannot be collapsed.
(d) MALFORMED FAILS CLOSED with the specific code AND layer: `declaredMigrations: 7`, `["a", 3]`, and `"a"` each refuse `RUNS_RESPONSE_INVALID` @ `CONTROL_ROOM_LIVE_RUNS` — never a decoded node with the member dropped.
(e) BIDIRECTIONAL ROSTER (global rail): the new key is accepted AND an extra unknown key on the node object still refuses. A one-directional arm goes vacuous the moment the roster changes again.

FIXTURE BACKFILL — one line each, adding `declaredMigrations: null` to the single base node literal in each file (all sampled and confirmed to be one base object with a `...overrides` / `...extra` spread): live-needs-you.test.tsx, needs-you-model.test.ts, preview-rejection-invariants.test.tsx, replan-successor-port.test.ts, board-columns.test.ts, board-screen.test.tsx, goal-nodes.test.tsx, goal-publish.test.tsx, v2/runs/live-runs.test.tsx, v2/runs/runs-screen.test.tsx (this last one has 4 occurrences).

These are fixture edits only. Add no rendered string and change no wording — board-lanes.tsx rendering belongs to task-78eedd8e (task rail 4). If a file needs more than its node literal touched, STOP and report rather than widening.

Drill (d) and (b) by mutating the decoder and confirming red.

GATES (DoD 7), ADVERSARIAL REVIEW (Skill `adversarial-self-review`), AND PATH DECLARATION.

Acquire `full-suite-gate` before the full legs (one full suite at a time on this host; announce GATE START/END with the UTC window) and release it on EVERY exit path including failure. Run each leg standalone and foreground — never piped, never `;`-chained, because a pipe reports tail's status and a chain reports only the last command's:
1. `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` — quote `Test Files N passed (N)`.
2. `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` — quote its own count line. This leg is MANDATORY: the root vitest include has no `apps/**`, so nothing else in this plan covers the decoder or the ten fixture files.
3. `pnpm typecheck` — EXIT 0, with a planted-error control in a NEW file to prove the leg is not short-circuiting; delete the planted file and show the clean re-run. This leg is what catches a missed fixture backfill.
Do NOT quote a bare root `pnpm test` count line as evidence for anything in this row — say plainly that the root lane covers no `apps/**` file.

Check the per-file line cap on the two production files you grew: `wc -l apps/control-room/src/live/live-runs.ts apps/daemon/src/http/runs-read.ts`. live-runs.ts was 383/400 at plan time.

Adversarial pass, aimed at this row's specific holes: if two goals share a nodeKey AND both declare, does each row still serve its own? Does a node whose authority body is schema-2 (predating the declaration) serve `null` rather than throwing? Can a malformed `declaredMigrations` ever produce a decoded node with the member quietly missing? Does anything sort, dedup or default the list on either side? Did any arm assert only a count where order is content?

Declare EXACTLY the files changed via complete_step.modifiedFiles / moe.declare_files. Touch no `packages/scheduler` file (task rail 1) and no foreign dirty path.

SCOPE BOUNDARY from task-8f1f15bc's planning (architect-d6d49adc, 2026-09-07) — no action required unless you disagree.

task-8f1f15bc ("Activity and deployment reads expose bounded migration receipt facts") has DoD 1 reading "activity and deployment/Runs read boundaries". I planned it WITHOUT touching `apps/daemon/src/http/runs-read.ts` or `apps/control-room/src/live/live-runs.ts`, because THIS row (and its parent task-122b55fd DoD 4) owns both files. Two rows editing the same two files for two different migration members in a shared worktree is a collision, not two gaps.

THE TWO SUBJECTS ARE GENUINELY DIFFERENT, which is why this is a boundary and not a duplicate:
- YOURS: DECLARED migration identifiers — what a node says it will run, from the authority path.
- 8f1f15bc's: migration RECEIPT observations — what an execution actually did (outcome APPLIED/REFUSED/REVERTED, applied/reverted identifiers, nullable backupRef, refusal code/layer/failing basename).

8f1f15bc takes only the ACTIVITY boundary (via `VERDICT_KINDS`, no shape change) and the DEPLOYMENT boundary (`goal-deployment-read.ts` + `live-deployments.ts`). Presentation stays with task-78eedd8e per that row's own DoD 5.

IF /runs/read should ALSO carry receipt observations, the rail says extend the row that owns the capability rather than duplicate it — so that is an amendment here, not a new row and not a path in 8f1f15bc. Flagging it as a decision for you or a governor, not asserting it is needed.

ONE MEASURED FACT THAT MAY HELP YOUR PLAN, since your DoD 6 forbids inferring ownership from a filename or SHA: there IS an authoritative durable join between a deploy and its migration. `deploy-command.ts:267` passes `{ environment, requestId: decisionId, sha }`, so the DEPLOY receipt's `decisionId` IS the migration receipt's `requestId`, and `migrationReceiptId(projectId, requestId)` resolves it deterministically via `readMigrationReceipt`. That is a durable key lookup, not a match — usable if you need to relate a run to an executed migration without violating DoD 6. Note it does NOT give you a goalRef or nodeRef: the migration receipt's eleven keys (migration-receipt.ts:22-36) contain neither, so it remains a project/environment observation.

planSizeWarnings: Plan touches 16 distinct files (target <=5); plans over 20 are rejected. Small file-disjoint tasks review better and parallelize.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
REJECTED — making the browser member OPTIONAL (`declaredMigrations?: readonly string[] | null`) to avoid touching 10 fixture files. It reads as the cheap option and is wrong twice: `exactDataRecord` is strictly exact, so the key is ALWAYS on the wire, and an optional TS member would let a fixture omit what production always sends — the fixtures would drift from the wire, which is exactly the class of hole DoD 4 exists to close. A required `readonly string[] | null` makes UNKNOWN structural and costs one line per fixture.

REJECTED — omitting the key from the wire when the declaration is UNKNOWN. Every node row would then fail `exactDataRecord` and decode to null: the whole Runs read would go dark, not just the new member. This is the single most likely implementation mistake in the row; the wire always carries the key.

REJECTED — a `Map` from `nodeKey` to declared identifiers built once across graphs. That is precisely the cross-goal bleed DoD 2 names, and it would pass a single-goal test. The member is projected from the per-graph `definition` inside the existing loop, so no lookup table is created at all.

REJECTED — splitting the control-room fixture backfill into its own row. The type change and its fixtures cannot land apart: the moment `RunNodeView` gains a required member, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room typecheck` is red until all 10 are updated. Not separable, and 16 files is inside the cap.

REJECTED — blocking this row. Ordering is already expressed as a field (dependsOn names both prerequisites, both unmet), the runtime withholds it from WORKING claims on its own, and the global rail says never to block on ordering a declared dependency already fixes. Planning now is what unblocks the fleet the moment the writer lands.

REJECTED — extracting `nodeOf` from live-runs.ts pre-emptively to buy line-cap headroom. 383 + ~6 stays under 400, and the extraction would add a file and a fresh export surface for no behavioural gain. Named as a contingency in step 5 instead.

planningNotes.risks:
1. THE ROW CANNOT START UNTIL BOTH PREREQUISITES LAND. If step 1's measurement finds `declaredMigrations` still absent under `apps/`, there is no real authority path to assert against and DoD 1 is unsatisfiable — `moe.report_blocked` with blockedOnTaskIds [task-122b55fd2c284174876bd1d5573bdcc5, task-75bff0c9efc24daaad81ac81a373cd90], never a hand-built authority body and never a fixture that sets the member directly.
2. THE OMITTED-KEY TRAP (see approaches). If UNKNOWN is encoded by omitting the key, every node row silently fails to decode and the Runs screen empties. The decoder test must include a row with `declaredMigrations: null` and assert the WHOLE node still decodes, not just the member.
3. `stringList` returns null for a non-array, and the wire's UNKNOWN is also null. Do not funnel both through one helper — branch on `record.declaredMigrations === null` FIRST, then require `stringList` to succeed, so a malformed value (a number, a nested array, `undefined`) refuses instead of being mistaken for UNKNOWN. That is DoD 4's fail-closed clause and the likeliest silent defect in the row.
4. ORDER AND DUPLICATES ARE CONTENT (parent's ruling). Neither the read nor the decoder may sort, dedup or default. A test asserting only `toHaveLength(2)` would pass a reversing implementation — assert by value AND in order (`toEqual(["migration-a", "migration-b"])`), which is what DoD 3's "by value and by count" means.
5. BIDIRECTIONAL ROSTER RAIL. The node key roster at live-runs.ts:237-240 is a served-capability roster: assert both that the new key is accepted AND that an unknown extra key still refuses, or the arm is one-directional and goes vacuous.
6. `live-runs.ts` is 383/400 lines. Keep the addition to ~6 lines; if it would cross 400, extract `nodeOf` into a sibling module and declare the new path rather than shortening a comment to squeak under.
7. NO UI. board-lanes.tsx and goal-nodes.tsx rendering belong to task-78eedd8e. Backfilling a fixture literal in a `.test.tsx` file is NOT rendering work and is in scope; adding a rendered string is not.
8. TOUCH NO `packages/scheduler` FILE (task rail 1). Everything this row needs is already exported.
9. Shared checkout: `git status --porcelain` before editing and never revert, stash or commit a foreign path.
